clue.text: Stray from on/off county, the first one to reach its bay

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a noun: a deviator is one who strays from the path

indicators.note: read as 'on' off, the little word is to be stripped away from the county

blocks.note: the English county in the south-west
Roman numeral one
A is the first letter of the alphabet
the part of Torbay, Devon's bay, that comes before 'bay'

explanation.surface: A wanderer leaves a county and is the first to arrive at its bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Torbay is the bay on the Devon coast, so 'its bay' points back to the same county; TOR is what you add to reach the word bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A deviator is a person or thing that departs from the usual course, so the clue's verb hints at the agent noun.

clue.text: Give up what will boost the personality?

definitions.note: a cryptic reading split as two words, 'for ego'

blocks.note: first meaning: renounce or go without
second reading: something done for the sake of one's self-image

explanation.surface: A self-help question about what to sacrifice in order to strengthen one's character.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as FOR EGO and it describes anything done to flatter the self; read whole it means to renounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Forego is a variant spelling of forgo, meaning to do without or relinquish something voluntarily.

clue.text: In past time I beat my wife? Then it's time for love

blocks.note: the confession turned round: he hit her
T is the abbreviation for time
love is nil, the zero shaped like O, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A shocking confession of domestic violence followed by a hope that romance will return.
explanation.walkthrough: The confession becomes HIT HER, then time and love supply T and O in that order to make HITHERTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto means up until now, so it describes what was so in time already past.

clue.text: Hatred is complex, but possible to follow

definitions.note: describes the answer rather than replacing it: a thread is something one can follow

indicators.note: something complex is tangled up, so the letters of the preceding word are knotted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hatred may be a complicated emotion, but its course can still be traced.
explanation.walkthrough: A thread, of an argument or a story, is a line you can follow, which is why the definition reads as an adjective phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: One follows the thread of a conversation or argument, tracing its continuous line from start to finish.

clue.text: Is solver on setter's side? Get it?

definitions.note: a cryptic reading: you the solver, me the setter

blocks.note: first reading: is the solver in agreement with the setter, asked by the setter
second meaning: do you understand what I am saying

explanation.walkthrough: The setter addresses the solver directly, so 'you' is the solver and 'me' the setter; the same question also asks whether one has followed an explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: The question checks whether a listener has understood, the same sense as the informal query asking whether someone follows.

clue.text: Gold for god, the creator

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Pagan worship trading gold to a deity who made the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The god looks like the creator, but the creator here is a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is the originator of a book or other work, the person who brings it into being.

clue.text: See 5
Quadrupedal current in Queen's building

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are put together afresh in another order

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
the word itself, the 's linking it to building

explanation.surface: A four-legged creature carries an electric current inside a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's building' looks like a palace, but the building is the reworking of the word plus the current.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine means relating to horses, which are four-footed animals, so the adjective for walking on four legs fits loosely.

clue.text: Lawrence, entertaining one on his own to dine, was killed by overwork

indicators.note: a host who is entertaining has guests inside the house, so the outer letters hold the rest

blocks.note: D. H. Lawrence, the novelist
taken as written
to eat is to dine
Lawrence's own first initial, used a second time

explanation.surface: D. H. Lawrence dines alone with a guest and is worked to death.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist's initials hold the guest and his meal, with his own D slipped in before the eating; an overworked phrase is said to be done to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done to death has been used or repeated so often that it is worn out, as if overworked.

clue.text: Punishment for lance-corporal, a good guy and mature

definitions.note: a cryptic definition: being stripped of a stripe is the punishment

blocks.note: a saint is a good person, abbreviated ST
ripe means fully developed

explanation.surface: A disciplined junior soldier who is both a decent chap and grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: A lance-corporal wears one stripe, so demoting him takes it away; the stripe itself is shorthand for that loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is the chevron badge of rank on a soldier's sleeve; losing one is a standard military demotion.

clue.text: Compound of oxygen and hydrogen source of pigment?

definitions.note: ochreous means of ochre, a natural pigment

indicators.note: in chemistry a compound combines elements, so the letters are mixed together here

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry question about which compound of oxygen and hydrogen yields a pigment.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxygen and hydrogen suggest water, but they are just two symbols added to the word source before mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy mineral used as yellow or brown pigment, and ochreous describes things containing or resembling it.

clue.text: See 22
Predominant elements in Yorkshire cricket?

blocks.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
Yorkshire was historically divided into three Ridings

explanation.surface: Asking which parts of Yorkshire's cricket team dominate.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order: the cricket unit first, then the Yorkshire division.
explanation.definitionFit: Overriding means more important than anything else, taking precedence, which is what predominant means.

clue.text: "No form, no win" will provide for us henceforth

indicators.note: the slogan's letters are said to provide something new, so they are rearranged to supply it

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A defeatist motto about being out of form, adopted as a rule for the future.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted slogan looks like a sporting saying, but its eleven letters are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: From now on in means starting at this moment and continuing into the future, the same as henceforth.

clue.text: Soften the report of the scandal of Thurber's Walter?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the answer is the sound of the phrase that follows

blocks.note: Walter Mitty is James Thurber's daydreaming hero, and -gate names a scandal after Watergate

explanation.surface: Playing down news of an affair involving a famous fictional fantasist.
explanation.walkthrough: Any scandal can be named with -gate after Watergate, so Walter Mitty's would be a Mitty-gate.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitigate is to make something less severe or painful, lessening its harshness, which is to soften it.

clue.text: I leave the odd diversion, usually leaving en masse

definitions.note: 'usually leaving' points to the usual collocation, leaving in droves

indicators.note: the letter departs, so it is taken out of the following word
odd means peculiar or out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letter that leaves
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller abandons a strange detour, as most people do when they depart together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' suggests taking alternate letters, but here it means the shortened word is rearranged; crowds are usually said to leave in droves.
explanation.definitionFit: In droves means in large numbers or crowds, like a drove of driven cattle, the same as all together en masse.

clue.text: Articles only for this girl

blocks.note: three articles in a row: an, the and a

explanation.surface: A girl whose name is made of nothing but little grammatical words.
explanation.walkthrough: The indefinite article an, the definite article the, and the indefinite a together spell the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a female given name, so it can stand for a particular girl referred to in the clue.

clue.text: Bird to ring, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this signals that the answer is said the same as the word described, though spelt differently

blocks.note: a signet is a ring bearing a seal

explanation.surface: Instructions for ringing a bird, as ornithologists tag them.
explanation.walkthrough: Birds are ringed for identification, so the surface reads as fieldwork, but the ring is a signet ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, a specific kind of bird.

clue.text: Top duplicator for footmen gains agreement among journalists: is this a threat or  ...

definitions.note: a cryptic definition continued into the next clue: the phrase can threaten or promise

indicators.note: topping something takes its head off, so the first letter of the brand goes
being among a group means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Roneo was a make of office stencil duplicator
foot is FT, and men are hes, males
editors, abbreviated
ay is an old word of assent

explanation.surface: An office copier for servants wins over the press, then a menacing question.
explanation.walkthrough: Roneo was a once-familiar British brand of office duplicator, and treating men as 'hes' is a setter's liberty. The definition runs on into 22: a threat or a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: One of these days means at some unspecified future time, said either as a warning or a vague undertaking.

clue.text: Speak about the Pole? Fancy!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speaking word goes round the other piece

blocks.note: to orate is to make a speech
N for the North Pole

explanation.surface: Delivering a speech about a Polish person, with a cry of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it is the North Pole, abbreviated N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, and fancy as an adjective means elaborate or highly ornamented.

clue.text: Make it possible to catch some elephants outside

indicators.note: some of a word means only part of it is used, here its opening letters
outside means on the exterior, so the partial word wraps round the catching word

blocks.note: the first three letters
to nab is to catch

explanation.surface: Arranging for hunters to capture several elephants in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to give the means or opportunity for something, so it renders an outcome possible.

clue.text: See 18
...  a promise of time coming from me to stand drinks to Marshal Tito?

annotation.answer: WHEN I GET AROUND TO IT

definitions.note: continues the definition begun in 18: a threat or a promise

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange in order, so the dictator's name is set out afresh

blocks.clueFragment: coming from me to stand drinks
blocks.note: what I say when it is my turn to buy: when I get a round
Marshal Tito, the Yugoslav leader

explanation.surface: A procrastinator promises to buy drinks for the Yugoslav leader some day.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshal looks like Tito's rank, but it tells you to arrange his name. Standing a round means buying drinks for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: When I get around to it is the classic vague assurance that something will be done at some unspecified later date.

clue.text: See 22
Clever is a student that's not depressed by Lawrence

indicators.note: not tells us the following idea is absent, so those letters are removed from the student

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
dented means pressed in, so dent stands for depress
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: A bright student cheered up, not brought low, by Lawrence's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Depressed suggests gloom, but it means dented, and DENT comes off the end of student. Lawrence here is T. E., not D. H. as in 8.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and quick to see an advantage, a close synonym of clever.

clue.text: His start in Eastwood meant he had a patron

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer: a client is one who has a patron

indicators.note: the start of a name is its first part, here the actor's given name and his surname's first letter
in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: his start, Eastwood's first name
the opening letter of the surname

explanation.surface: The actor-director's early career depended on a powerful backer.
explanation.walkthrough: Clint Eastwood's first name opens his career, and the first letter of his surname is inserted into it.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a client was a dependant under the protection of a patron, so having a patron makes one a client.
